title: Size bound for an unfolded gate
statement: Let $g$ be a gate whose argument list has no repetitions and, if $g$ is a NOT gate, has length one. Let $t$ assign a Boolean circuit tree to each vertex and polarity, and suppose that for every vertex the assigned circuit has the same size at both polarities. For either polarity $p$, the size of the circuit obtained by unfolding $g$ at $p$ is at most one plus the sum of the sizes of the circuits assigned to its arguments at polarity $p$.
hypotheses_covered: The gate's arguments are pairwise distinct
A NOT gate has exactly one argument
The tree assignment has polarity-independent size at every vertex
